blocking_findings.issue: Human-trigger classification pre-empts approved curated FAQ answers, making deliberately-aliased business FAQs unreachable (unnecessary refusal of approved company facts).
blocking_findings.evidence: safety.py HUMAN_TRIGGER_PATTERN includes 'bonded|insured|warranty|warranties'. Agent.ask() short-circuits kind=='human' to fallback before _answer() ever checks exact question/tag matches. ChatService._respond() branches on kind=='human' to HUMAN before _curated_ids(). Yet chat_service._curated_ids alias_map deliberately maps 'are you insured'->faq-032, 'do you have bonding capacity'->faq-048, 'are you bonded'->faq-048. A homeowner asking 'Are you bonded and insured?' is classified human and gets the generic HUMAN/FALLBACK even though the owner approved curated answers and added aliases. No test exercises an FAQ whose question text hits a human trigger; the fixture question 'What is the fixture service?' is benign, so this dead path is untested.
blocking_findings.recommendation: In Agent.ask() and ChatService._respond(), check normalized exact-question/unique-tag match (and the chat alias_map) BEFORE applying the human-trigger fallback. Exact curated answers are approved strings and serving them does not relax any safeguard; the human fallback should apply only when no approved match exists. Keep paid model path unchanged and keep the USD1/month cap.
blocking_findings.regression_test: Add a fixture FAQ with question 'Are you bonded and insured?' (status source_verified, runtime_eligible true) and assert agent.ask({question:'Are you bonded and insured?'}) returns status answered with the exact curated string and no provider call; assert ChatService._respond returns answered via _curated_ids for alias 'are you bonded'.

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Reconsider the blanket numeral ban (r'[\d$%]') in _validate_general_answer, e.g., permit numerals not adjacent to $, %, phone, or step patterns.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: Useful tailored plain-language answers often need harmless numbers (measurements, counts, code-cycle references). Today any digit forces plan rejection and a needs_review fallback, degrading the novel-question value the feature exists for, as noted in the unnecessary-refusal review goal. This is safe-direction over-refusal, not an exploit.

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Align source URL validation: _approved requires sources startswith('https://') while agent.valid_source and docs/review-workflow.md allow http on approved hosts.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: An approved FAQ with an http source URL would answer correctly over /ask but be silently downgraded to needs_help in chat. Either restrict valid_source to https everywhere or accept valid_source() result in chat; current behavior is an undocumented inconsistency, not a hole (chat direction is stricter).

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Update the final paragraph: tests are no longer 'planned'; 49 provider-mocked tests ran OK. Keep the honest caveats (no live provider, no browser QA) but remove the stale 'no pass counts asserted' line now contradicted by the recorded run.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: Documentation should not understate or contradict actual verification state; the current wording conflicts with the supplied test transcript.

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Add end-to-end tests for the homeowner-usefulness cases: 'white roof vs black roof heat gain' reaching guidance-roof when no API key is configured; 'how long have you been doing this' answered from faq-002 while 'when was the company founded' falls back (40-years-team-experience vs company-age separation); 'what is your phone number/email' answered from faq-028; 'male vs female threaded fittings' and 'church facility remodel' classified safe and reaching guidance/model; WOSB and accessibility answered, not refused.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: classify_question and the alias_map cover these in code, but only classify/screen parity is tested; the full ask/chat path for these exact ordinary questions is unverified, and B1 shows pre-emption bugs hide precisely here.

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Consider a narrow allowlist exception in _validate_general_answer's procedural-imperative regex so common safe verbs after enumeration words (e.g., 'Generally, use ...' mid-sentence is already allowed; sentence-initial 'Use' is not) are handled deliberately, and log the specific rejection reason in the private event for review tuning.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: Legitimate high-level answers often begin sentences with 'Use' or 'Replace'; silent fallback with reason 'invalid_model_selection' hides how often validation, not the model, caused refusal. Observability aids review without relaxing output rules.

positive_evidence: Novel general questions demonstrably reach the mocked LLM and return tailored validated text: test_real_general_answer_grounded_and_exact_faq_byte_identical shows a general_answer plan passing _validate_plan/_materialize_plan into the public answer labeled 'General construction guidance:', with empty faq_ids/sources, model_used=MODEL, and 200 microUSD settled.

Model general answers are NOT rejected by cache/proof reconstruction or ChatService: test_cached_general_validated_avoids_second_model_call proves validated plans are cached under catalog_hash and replayed without a second model call; test_forged_proofs_rejected_by_rebuild_and_chat_approval and test_raw_general_rejected_and_valid_general_only_proof_approved prove general-only proofs pass ChatService._approved while forged IDs, duplicated evidence, changed answers, and attacker sources return needs_help.

Legitimate sensitive-context terms are allowed while social judgments are blocked: test_unsafe_inputs_blocked_before_provider_and_legitimate_terms_allowed and test_classify_screen_contracts cover white/black roof colors, WOSB, accessibility/grab bars, male/female threaded fittings, sex bolts, church remodel; hateful/discriminatory, NSFW, injection, and credential cases fall back with zero provider calls.

Business-fact separation holds: generated answers containing 'CCC', 'we/our', prices, phone numbers, guarantees, engineering sizing, numbered steps, or legal-compliance claims are all rejected to FALLBACK (test_generated_general_rejects_company_facts_credentials_prices_engineering_promises); company facts flow only through approved evidence IDs.

No invented quotes/availability/engineering: unsupported and human-classified questions return FALLBACK/HUMAN without provider calls (test_unsupported_claims_stop_before_provider, test_unsafe_agent_questions_fallback_without_provider); HUMAN_SUFFIX makes no commitment.

No-API/exhausted-budget behavior is honest and useful: test_exhausted_budget_exact_and_static_guidance_free_without_model and test_exhausted_budget_never_calls_paid_model_but_exact_faq_still_works show exact FAQs and deterministic static guidance still serve with zero paid calls, novel queries degrade to fallback, and uncertain provider failures retain reservations within the USD1/month cap (test_uncertain_provider_failure_and_missing_cost_keep_reservation, StoreTests budget suite).

Professional concise fallbacks: FALLBACK and chat HUMAN strings are source-limited, contain no fabricated contact promises, and review queuing is bounded and deduplicated (StoreTests.test_daily_limit_and_review_dedup_caps).
49 provider-mocked tests pass with a network guard backstop forbidding real outbound calls.
limitations: All model, pricing, and email traffic is mocked; real deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash schema compliance with the new conversation-plan JSON (general_answer key) and OpenRouter max_price routing is unverified, so live tailored-answer quality and real-world refusal rates are unknown.

The production 50-entry FAQ snapshot content was not supplied for review; alias_map targets (faq-001/002/003/004/028/029/032/046/047/048) cannot be confirmed against actual approved questions/answers, and B1's impact depends on real snapshot wording.

chat_http.py, chat_mail.py, network.py, dashboard.py, digest.py, faq_pages.py and the production data/faq.json were not in the supplied source; chat transport auth/CORS behavior is reviewed only through ChatService.

Regex classification (hate/NSFW/injection) is inherently evadable; tests cover listed cases only. README itself disclaims satisfaction/relevance guarantees; no live HTTPS, Railway volume, browser accessibility, or email delivery was asserted or tested.
